reasoning: This is a snap hook that clips over a 1.2 mm ledge on a lid, opened often. It's functional, light load, indoor. What makes it succeed or fail: the hook profile must be dimensionally accurate so it sits flush on the ledge and releases cleanly with repeated use; the ceiling under the hook arm (the 90° overhang) cannot print without support; the part is small and slender with a small bed contact area, so it's prone to lifting. The section is thin (1.87 mm) and the walls dominate the structure. I loaded all seven reference groups because the part touches adhesion (small footprint, slender), supports (ceiling overhang, bridge), layer height (must fit the 1.2 mm ledge), and speed/cooling (thin sections, small layer times at the reduced layer height).

changes.reason: A 90° overhang is a ceiling — it cannot print unsupported at any layer height within the bound. The ceiling is the underside of the hook arm that clips over the ledge; it is inherent to the hook's function and cannot be chamfered to 45° without destroying the clip geometry. This is not a design-out case; support is required.
The Sponsor's practice is tree supports whenever supports are used. The code bound allows only tree(auto). Set accordingly.

Bed contact is 128 mm², under the 200 mm² trigger. Slenderness is 2.8×, over the 2.5× trigger. Both adhesion conditions are met. auto_brim calculates a width from geometry and print parameters; for a small, tall part with a narrow footprint it will add enough perimeter to resist lifting during the print without a fixed-width brim that might be over- or under-sized.

The hook's profile where it engages the 1.2 mm ledge is a fine curved surface that must fit. At 0.20 mm the ledge height spans 6 layers; the staircase on the hook's curve will make the fit coarse and may prevent a clean release on repeated opening. At 0.12 mm the same 1.2 mm spans 10 layers, a noticeably smoother profile. 0.12 mm is within the wiki's optimal range (20–80% of 0.4 mm nozzle = 0.08–0.32 mm) and within the machine bound. Secondary benefit: the 10 mm² bridge spans less vertical distance per layer, reducing sag.

design_notes: The 90° ceiling under the hook arm is the snap geometry itself — it clips over the 1.2 mm ledge. It cannot be chamfered to 45° or redesigned as a support-free overhang without changing the hook's function. Tree support is the correct solution; it is not a missed design-out opportunity.
The 10 mm² bridge (flat downward face) will also fall within the tree support's reach at the 30° threshold; it does not need a separate decision.
